newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends down on Tokyo's fall.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends down on Tokyo's fall.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices closed slightly lower after another uneventful session as consumer demand stayed absent, traders said.
They said with no new factors to trade on, the market took its cue from a weaker trend in Tokyo.
The death of China's paramount leader Deng Xiaoping was not a factor in the market, traders said.

"Nobody is talking about it. The market is very dull and featureless," said one trader. He said price movements were likely to be limited as sellers might hold back in anticipation of tighter supply during the wintering period.
At the close, benchmark March RSS1 buyer was quoted by the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board at 304 cents ($1.22) a kg, down half cent from Wednesday.
March SMR 20 buyer fell a cent at 298 cents ($1.20).
Trading houses offered the SMR 20 at 298 cents a kg, SMR CV at 360, SMR L at 340, SMR 5 at 308, SMR 10 at 299 and drum latex FOB at 239.
The INRO five-day moving average was 234.72 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on Feb 19 against 234.97 on Feb 18. The daily indicator price was 234.35 versus 235.27.
